articles.title: F1 in Rwanda: Why deal for race in Africa is also controversial
articles.summary: Formula 1 will return to Africa in the early 2030s, but Rwanda's deal to stage a race has prompted accusations of sportswashing against the country.
articles.body:
Formula 1 will return to Africa for the first time in a generation after Rwanda agreed a 10-year contract to stage a race, with the sport's governing body (FIA) keen to create a "lasting legacy".

The event - to be called the African Grand Prix - will be held on a new, purpose-built circuit in Bugesera, 25 miles south of the capital Kigali, with the first edition in the "early 2030s".

For Rwandan President Paul Kagame, the ambition is to "pave the way" for other F1 races on the continent.

However, the announcement has drawn criticism from some quarters amid allegations of sportswashing and questions around the East African country's human rights record.

Africa has not hosted an F1 race since 1993, and the clamour to return to the continent has been growing in recent years - with seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton among those leading the calls.

Morocco was the first African nation to host a Grand Prix in 1958 and 23 races were then held in South Africa between 1962 and 1993.

President Kagame said it was "an honour and privilege" for Rwanda to be chosen for its return.

"This partnership is long overdue but it is a success and a milestone for the entire continent - especially for African fans," he added.

South Africa had been keen to secure its own F1 race, and sports minister Gayton McKenzie remains bullish about his country's hopes of emulating Rwanda.

"They have worked on it longer than SA and deserve it," he posted on X.

"Remember though that one country, Italy, has had two [F1 races] a year, and some react like a continent of [54] countries can only get one. SA will get F1, even before 2030."

Rwanda to host F1's first race in Africa since 1993

A 'landmark' moment - why has Rwanda been chosen to host F1?

The year of the first African Grand Prix in the 2030s, and its timing in the calendar, are yet to be announced.

F1 is likely to want to avoid holding the race in Rwanda's main rainy season of March to May, while there is a shorter, less disruptive, rainy season from October to November.

The sport is committed to keeping the season at no more than 24 races.

Former F1 driver Alex Wurz will be involved in the design of the circuit, which is due to use the undulating Rwandan landscape to produce a track with a natural flow and elevation changes of nearly 200m to challenge drivers.

Could the race boost African participation?

Jody Sheckter remains the only African to win the F1 Drivers' Championship, triumphing in 1979 with Ferrari.

"It's so expensive to get in," the South African told Newsday on the BBC World Service when discussing whether or not the race in Rwanda could open the door to more drivers from the continent.

"I built my own cars at the beginning. You can't do that anymore."

Africans hoping for a career in motorsport have previously had to chase their dream overseas, according to fellow driver Axcil Jefferies, who has previously competed in Formula 2.

But the Zimbabwean believes that could now change.

"F1 coming to Africa will highlight to everyone what a big industry motorsport is," he said.

"All the elements will inspire the youth, whether that's to come in as an engineer, as a mechanic, as drivers, as team coordinators."

South African presenter Kriya Gangiah, who hosts SuperSport's F1 Extra Africa Trackside podcast, is also hopeful of a boost in the number of female fans and drivers in Africa.

"The more you see something and the more that is present in your world, the more you take interest in it," she said.

"Being in paddocks in South Africa, you're seeing the amount of women that are making it into the sport and are actually doing really well. A lot of the girls are giving the guys a proper run for their money."

Allegations of sportswashing - hosting sporting events to improve a country's international reputation - have long been levelled against Rwanda.

Securing an F1 race is part of the country's wider strategy to increase tourism, international investment, services and entertainment.

The country has hosted the Basketball Africa League finals in all but one year since 2021 and staged cycling's World Road Championships last year, the first time the event had been held in Africa.

Visit Rwanda has either sponsored or had partnerships with Arsenal, Bayern Munich and Paris St-Germain, although its sleeve sponsorship of the Gunners ended this year after drawing criticism from supporter groups.

Meanwhile, Rwanda's central African neighbour, the Democratic Republic of Congo, has filed a case against the country at the International Court of Justice, accusing it of breaching multiple international treaties covering genocide prevention, racial discrimination, women's rights and torture.

Human Rights Watch previously said that "the space for freedom of expression" and "political autonomy" is shrinking in the country.

"Rwanda is buying into the world's biggest sports to polish its image and deflect from its appalling human rights record," said Amnesty International UK's head of campaigns Felix Jakens.

"A 10-year Grand Prix 'presented by Visit Rwanda' is a sportswashing prize for the Rwandan authorities."

The Rwandan government has dismissed such accusations, with chief tourism officer Irene Murerwa calling them "a distraction' from the "amazing and outstanding achievements the country has made" when previously challenged by BBC Sport Africa.

"The benefits trickle down to every Rwandan," she said in December 2024. "Hosting F1 would be another step in our journey to becoming a world-class destination."

F1 is not blind to issues around sportswashing, with several countries on the calendar accused of utilising the strategy - not least Saudi Arabia.

F1's own charter commits it to "respecting internationally recognised human rights in its operations globally" and emphasises the importance of understanding and monitoring potential human rights impacts and engaging with stakeholders.

A statement in the context of the Rwandan announcement said: "We have the opportunity to inspire and bring the passion of F1 to 100 million people across Africa and sport can be a positive force for good."

However, it has still drawn criticism from human rights organisations, with Amnesty International's Jakens believing the organisation's words "ring hollow".

"It should use its influence with the Rwandan authorities to push for change, rather than lend its brand to a PR exercise," he said.

When asked about the sportswashing accusations levelled against Rwanda when it was bidding to host a race, FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem told BBC Sport Africa: "When people cannot get what they want, they always blame it on sportswashing.

"I honestly don't care about what they say."

articles.title: Quiles: "No he venido al Mundial a ganar un título y ya está”
articles.standfirst: Entrevista MARCA al campeón de Moto3
articles.summary: Entrevista MARCA al campeón de Moto3
articles.body: Agotado, pero con la sonrisa instalada en su cara de forma perenne. Así estaba Máximo Quiles (Murcia, 2008), recién aterrizado de Indonesia, donde se proclamó campeón de Moto3. El ‘Gladiator’ lo festejó a lo grande incluso con Marc Márquez, su mentor. Ahora, le esperan nuevos retos, pero los afronta con la misma ambición. PREGUNTA. Ya todo el mundo sabe que su nombre le viene por la película ‘Gladiator’. ¿Cuántas veces la ha visto? RESPUESTA. La he visto unas cuantas, la verdad. No sé cuántas, pero bastantes; en los aviones me gusta verla, me la sé bastante. P. ¿Te la pones para motivarte? R. Bueno, siempre está esa motivación. Al final, motiva. El nombre viene de ahí, entonces le da una motivación. P. Máximo Décimo Meridio y tú lo lograste con tu décima victoria. Quedan cinco carreras, si no se suspende Qatar, con lo que tiene a tiro el récord de más victorias en la categoría (125 y Moto3), que logró David Alonso, con 14. ¿Se puede? R. Hombre, son palabras mayores. Él lo hizo muy bien. Lo veo difícil, pero lo voy a dar todo para que sea así. Yo creo que si estamos concentrados, podemos lograr más victorias. No sé cuántas, pero intentaré que sean unas cuantas más. P. El décimo también es lo que persigue Marc Márquez. ¿Cómo lo ve? ¿Es posible que lo gane? R. Sí, sin ninguna duda. Mentalmente, está más fuerte que nunca. Físicamente, no tanto por el hombro, pero ya saca él el talento, así que lo veo fuerte y está con ganas. P. ¿Qué te dijo exactamente para felicitarte? R. Al final, él me ha felicitado por el campeonato del mundo, por todo el trabajo. Yo también estoy contento con él por la parte que él ha hecho conmigo. Siempre es bonito que se logre un título y él estaba muy feliz por todo. P. Siempre te preguntamos qué consejos te da Marc. Yo te pregunto: ¿Qué consejos le das tú a él? R. No, yo no me atrevo. Es que en los grandes premios no lo veo. Él tiene su movida; yo, la mía y estamos concentrados. P. Tu próximo reto es Moto2. No tiene ningún test hasta febrero. ¿Te gustaría subirte antes? R. La verdad es que me gustaría antes, pero así la coges aún con más ganas. No sé ni cómo va eso de los entrenamientos ni cuándo puedo hacerlo, pero bueno, cuando tenga que ser, me subiré. P. Tú eres un piloto al que no le importa crear expectativas altas, decir que le va a ir bien desde el principio en Moto2. ¿Por qué? R. Bueno, no lo sé. No me he subido todavía. Es muy difícil, a la gente le cuesta. Es la categoría más difícil, yo diría. Va a ser difícil el comienzo. Habrá que estar muy concentrado, trabajar con el equipo y con todo y ya irán saliendo las cosas. Supongo que irá todo bien y podré dar buenas guerras. P. Marc, estos días, decía que te ha ido todo muy rodado en el Mundial, que no iba mal si pasabas por momentos difíciles para valorar otras cosas y sacar otra motivación. ¿Qué te parece? R. Sí que he pasado por momentos difíciles. Al final, en Inglaterra me lesioné, en mitad de temporada, en un momento importante. Volví y volví a ganar. Todos esos momentos que han sido difíciles; luego, en los entrenamientos, que hay cosas que no se ven, estoy sufriendo y me toca sacar de otros sitios. Eso no se ve, pero está ahí siempre. Siempre hay momentos difíciles. P. ¿Por qué eres tan ambicioso? R. Yo tengo expectativas bajas, normalmente. Antes de los fines de semana, yo me pongo expectativas bajas. Siempre digo que no sé cómo va a ir ahí. Las expectativas son bajas, pero cuando sé que puedo tenerlas altas, las tengo altas. P. Pero tú no te cortas al decir que vas a aspirar a cosas grandes, que van a llegar cosas grandes. R. Sí, es que no puedo decir que no. No he venido aquí a pasarme al Mundial y a ganar un título y ya está. Yo quiero ir a por más. Entonces, siempre son altas, pero es para lo que he venido, para conseguir cosas grandes y lo daré todo para intentar conseguirlo. Son altas, pero en los momentos que toca, tengo las expectativas bajas. P. Has demostrado que llevas la presión bastante bien, ¿no? R. Sí. Siempre está la presión. La realidad es que la presión a veces te hace cometer errores; a mí me ha hecho cometer errores de vez en cuando. Está bien tenerla, pero tampoco mucho tiempo, si no te satura mucho. P. ¿Llegarás a rodar en la misma categoría, en MotoGP, con Marc? Está difícil, porque él firmo dos años y a ti, en teoría, te quedan dos en Moto2, ¿no? R. Nunca se sabe. A lo mejor él se ve inspirado y quiere hacer más años y apuntar a más títulos; no lo sé. O a lo mejor yo llego y subo. Yo voy a estar centrado en mis objetivos, hacer mis años en Moto2, con cabeza, intentar no sufrir tanto, porque será difícil y ya está. P. En MotoGP te deberías encontrar con otro murciano joven: Pedro Acosta. ¿Te ves luchando con él muchos años? R. Vamos a ir paso a paso. Todavía estoy en Moto3, me quedan dos años en Moto2; él ya está haciendo cosas grandes en MotoGP y viene también gente muy joven. Ahora, van a subir a MotoGP Dani (Holgado), David (Alonso), Izan (Guevara)... muchos pilotos muy rápidos. Entonces, habrá que ver cómo se dan de palos ellos y ojalá yo también llegue y esté al nivel de lograr victorias. P. Y por debajo también vienen: Brian Uriarte, Carlos Cano, Álvaro Lucas... R. Sí, hay cantera murciana y española. Se van a cansar de nosotros, de vernos ahí arriba a los españoles. P. En su día, Aspar premió a Pecco Bagnaia, cuando estaba en Moto3, con dejarle rodar con una MotoGP. ¿Te gustaría que te dieran un premio así? R. ¿Sí? No lo sabía. El problema está en que Aspar ahora no tiene equipo en MotoGP, si no ya lo hubiese dicho yo. Me encantaría, por supuesto, pero vamos a ir paso a paso. De momento, en cada momento lo que toque y ya veremos. P. Bueno. Álex Márquez también llevó una Honda y Marc tiene unas cuantas. ¿Te podía dejar alguna algún día? R. Uff. Peligroso. Igual la estrellaría. P. ¿Te gustaría alguna moto en concreto de MotoGP para cuando llegues? R. Eso es lejano. No lo sé. Si el día de mañana, tengo que subir y la moto que funciona ahora no funciona... No se piensa eso. Yo tengo que ir año a año. En Moto2, ahora tengo un objetivo grande, va a ser difícil. No pienso en eso, cuando tenga que llegar, llegará. P. Aquella prueba de Bagnaia llegó por una apuesta de Pecco con Gino Borsoi. ¿Tú te había hecho alguna apuesta por si ganabas el título de Moto3? R. Sí, algo hay, con CFMoto, también, algún buggy. Les dije que si ganaba el título que me dieran un buggy. Hay cosas. P. ¿Y promesas? ¿Habías hecho alguna promesa por si ganabas el título? R. Yo, no, pero dentro del equipo hay promesas que se hicieron entre ellos. Dani Barba fuma y habló con un amigo que si ganaba, tenía que dejar de fumar; ahora va a tener que hacerlo. Hay cosas.

articles.title: Lewis Hamilton: Has trust broken down between Ferrari driver and team's pit wall after Singapore GP issues?
articles.summary: Listen to the latest episode of The F1 Show podcast as Simon Lazenby, Bernie Collins and Karun Chandhok look back at all the big talking points from the Singapore Sprint weekend; watch every session of the United States GP in Austin on October 23-25, live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
Hamilton finished finish sixth instead of a likely third in last Sunday's race after not heeding a call from the team's pit wall to stop under a lap-39 Virtual Safety Car.

On team radio after the race following his struggle on worn tyres, Hamilton apologised for "my call" around the strategy, a position he subsequently reiterated on social media when he admitted he had learned a "painful lesson" by choosing "a strategy that ultimately didn't deliver".

It was the second weekend in a row that post-race debate around Ferrari had centred on race strategy.

At the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia the week before, Ferrari's drivers slipped to the back of the field in the twice-delayed race's early stages after the team had been among those to make the mistake of starting on slick tyres when the track was too wet.

Hamilton later said the process around that call, which he had questioned at the time, had prompted a "huge discussion" after the race .

Hamilton eventually fought back to an impressive third place at Sepang after deciding to stay on the slicks longer than team-mate Charles Leclerc, a gamble aided by the timely appearance of the Safety Car as the track dried.

So after further issues in Singapore, this time with Hamilton overriding Ferrari's request to pit under the VSC, the latest edition of the The F1 Show podcast included analysis on the situation at the Scuderia...

Has trust broken down over strategy calls?

Sky Sports F1's Bernie Collins, a former head of race strategy at Aston Martin, was first asked whether Singapore was evidence that the trust between Hamilton and the Ferrari pit wall had broken down.

"Lewis started on the medium tyre, which is one of the things he actually came out and said he thought in hindsight was the wrong decision, but was his decision," said Collins.

"He decided to go that way strategically at the beginning of the race.

"He stops earlier than everybody else so instantly when we're watching at home, we're thinking, 'okay, he's probably on a two-stop here' because he's the first of any of the cars really to stop.

"He puts on that soft tyre. Then they get this perfect opportunity with the virtual safety car to stop again, take another set of soft tyres. You could see the soft was a better tyre and you could see that it was going to be much faster to put a new set on.

"On the coverage at home, we didn't hear any call from Ferrari to box Lewis, but we don't hear a lot of the calls that happen. Fred [Vasseur] obviously came out afterwards and said, yes, they did call him, Lewis missed the entry or ignored the call, whichever way you want to think about it.

"But someone of Lewis's stature doesn't forget to do a pit stop. So let's say it's a decision to not take the pit entry or the call didn't come in time or whatever. But that was crucial, I think, to the race at that point.

"If we go back a week, we had the same sort of lack of trust, for want of another word, in Malaysia."

After Ferrari's tyre choice at the start in Malaysia saw their drivers fall more than a minute off the lead, Hamilton's decision from the car to cut their losses and wait it out on the slicks ultimately paid dividends.

Collins added: "That shows, more globally, that Lewis isn't trusting that Ferrari team.

"He's questioning their decisions and in this sort of quick-decision VSC moment, there's not the time to have all the back and forth about what he thinks or why he thinks it or doesn't think it.

"But it's very difficult from a pit wall and Lewis's side to then think, 'okay, last week I questioned them. I think I was correct. This week I'm going to question them, maybe I'm correct or incorrect.'

"And then there was opportunity later on, I think, even after they missed the VSC, to do a full pit stop and still be able to beat Piastri and they didn't take that either.

"There was the decision then to string it out and hope for another safety car.

"There were lots of decisions that should have been done differently and they should be having a very difficult conversation between Lewis and his engineers, or the strategy team or Fred [Vasseur], whoever needs to be involved, to say, 'where is the trust?

'When we make these decisions, what is the protocol for how that decision is taken and why?'"

Do Ferrari need to give Hamilton more information in the car earlier?

Collins believes that, generally, drivers do need to defer to the pit wall around such decisions given a team's strategists have a fuller picture of what is going on in the race.

However, she used an example from her time at Aston Martin with four-time world champion Sebastian Vettel as showing how teams can also give drivers more information leading up to pit stops.

"In my opinion, yes, [drivers] should [defer to the pit wall]," said Collins. "They're the people with the most information. They're the people with the big picture.

"However, there's another band of thought that says the driver is the most expensive sensor in the car. And I often had situations with Sebastian Vettel, who was very strong strategically, where we ended up starting to give him pit stop information earlier than we would give another driver in order to give him a sort of right to reply.

"If your driver regularly questions strategy, then you need to maybe give them the information.

"Many teams, lots and lots of teams in the situation that Ferrari were in, five laps before the safety car would have said, 'if there's a safety car now, we will take it and double stack the cars'. And that gives Lewis a chance to say, 'I think that's right, I think that's wrong'.

"You've a bit of a discussion about it. Yes, you're giving away information to other teams, which people don't want to do, but you're making the right decision for you and that is your P1 goal. So they need to bring the conversation forward if there's going to be a back and forth."

What are the lessons for both Hamilton and Ferrari?

Fellow Sky Sports F1 pundit and former driver Karun Chandhok believes "they've got to have some sort of reset" in terms of how they approach strategy discussions and decisions at Ferrari.

"Lewis was annoyed with the way Ferrari played that whole race," said Chandhok.

"If you look at it, he started on the medium tyre. Of the top-seven finishers, he was the only one to start on the medium tyre, yet he pitted first. They were clearly unhappy with his pace on the medium. We know it was a less preferred tyre, so they tried to get him off that tyre quickly. Fine.

"But then you have to look at the overall race time and they didn't look at that. They put him out behind Leclerc and then he sat there getting annoyed [at] the fact that he's not getting past Leclerc, and they didn't explain to either driver, that they need a swap. They didn't do a good job in that phase of the race.

"So then you've got Lewis who's now three seconds behind Charles annoyed that he's not been allowed to get in front. The VSC comes out, Charles boxes and he thinks, 'well, I'm going to have free air. I'm going to go for it.'

"He's not thinking of the big picture of the race and that's why I think the strategy team needed to say to him, 'Lewis, your tyres are 21 laps old now, you are going to get passed. You're going to drop like a stone when it comes to pace with all these people.'

"Leclerc didn't have new soft tyres but he had a set that had done one run in qualy, and you could just see, he came out of the pits and was two seconds a lap faster than Lewis when the VSC cleared.

"And that's where any driver has to trust and believe their strategy team and take the inputs and make that decision. But, equally, it's on the team to explain the big picture to the driver and navigate the whole thing and I don't think Ferrari did a good job across the whole race there."

articles.title: Formula 1: Red Bull's Laurent Mekies has contract extended to 2031
articles.summary: Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies, who replaced Christian Horner at the F1 team, has his contract extended until the end of 2031.
articles.body:
Red Bull have extended the contract of team principal Laurent Mekies until the end of 2031.

The Frenchman has led the team since he replaced Christian Horner following the Briton's sacking in the summer of 2025 after 20 years in charge.

After a difficult start to the 2026 season, Red Bull have improved their car to the extent that Max Verstappen has taken dominant victories in the last two races, in Malaysia and Singapore.

A statement attributed to the two main shareholders of Red Bull, Thai Chalerm Yoovidhya and Austrian Mark Mateschitz, said: "Laurent has played a crucial role in guiding the team through an important period of transition while maintaining the competitive spirit and the Red Bull principles that define us.

"This extension reflects our confidence in his leadership and our shared belief in the long-term vision of the team.

"We are ambitious about what lies ahead and we are committed to building on this momentum together."

The move comes less than two months after Verstappen extended his own contract with Red Bull by two years to the end of 2030 after a period of uncertainty over his future.

Verstappen's two victories came in the wake of an interview Horner gave to the Times in which he claimed Red Bull had "lost its mojo, its presence, its vibe".

Oliver Mintzlaff, who is in charge of the Red Bull F1 programme in his role as chief executive officer of corporate projects and investments, said: "Laurent has demonstrated outstanding leadership since returning to the Red Bull family. He combines technical expertise, strategic thinking, and a deep understanding of what makes our team successful.

"Just as importantly, he embodies the values and mentality that define the Red Bull way: courage, teamwork, determination, and an unrelenting desire to compete at the highest level.

"Continuity in leadership is a key ingredient for sustained success."

Mekies said: "I am incredibly proud to continue this journey with Red Bull Racing, and I would like to thank Chalerm, Mark, and Oliver, the entire team, and everyone involved for the trust they have placed in the project.

"What makes this team special is the way everyone comes together in pursuit of the same goal, and I feel privileged to work alongside such a talent and committed group every day."

articles.title: Laurent Mekies: Red Bull team principal signs contract extension to 2031 and vows recent wins 'only the beginning'
articles.summary: Red Bull announce extended five-year contract for team boss Laurent Mekies, who replaced Christian Horner in the role last season; watch every session of the United States GP in Austin on October 23-25, live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
Mekies joined the team from sister outfit Racing Bulls in July 2025 after Christian Horner was sacked following 20 years in charge.

News of Mekies' contract renewal comes in the wake of Red Bull claiming their first two wins of the season, both courtesy of Max Verstappen, over the past fortnight in Malaysia and Singapore.

They are fourth in the Constructors' Championship but have closed to within seven points of third-placed McLaren in what is shaping up to be a very competitive end to their first year as an engine manufacturer.

Verstappen extended his Red Bull contract to 2030 in August, while Isack Hadjar was also handed a contract renewal into 2027 after impressing in his first season at Milton Keynes.

In a joint statement announcing Mekies' extended deal, Red Bull shareholders Chalerm Yoovidhya and Mark Mateschitz said: "The strength of Red Bull has always come from its people and from creating an environment where talented individuals can achieve extraordinary things together.

"Laurent has played a crucial role in guiding the team through an important period of transition while maintaining the competitive spirit and the Red Bull principles that define us.

"This extension reflects our confidence in his leadership and our shared belief in the long term vision of the team.

"We are ambitious about what lies ahead and we are committed to building on this momentum together."

Mekies, who has also previously worked at Ferrari and the FIA, said: "I am incredibly proud to continue this journey with Oracle Red Bull Racing, and I would like to thank Chalerm, Mark, and Oliver [Mintzlaff], the entire team, and everyone involved for the trust they have placed in the project.

"What makes this team special is the way everyone comes together in pursuit of the same goal, and I feel privileged to work alongside such a talented and committed group every day.

"Together, with Pierre Wache's and Ben Hodgkinson's teams playing a central role in shaping our future, we have a strong platform for the years ahead, and we genuinely believe this is only the beginning.

"As we look ahead, we will continue to embrace the principles that define us: being free in our thinking, fast in our actions and bold in our decisions."

Oliver Mintzlaff, Red Bull's CEO of corporate projects and investments, also hailed the 49-year-old's Mekies' leadership qualities.

"Laurent has demonstrated outstanding leadership since returning to the Red Bull family," he said.

"He combines technical expertise, strategic thinking, and a deep understanding of what makes our team successful. Just as importantly, he embodies the values and mentality that define the Red Bull way: courage, teamwork, determination, and an unrelenting desire to compete at the highest level.

"Continuity in leadership is a key ingredient for sustained success, and we are delighted that Laurent will continue to lead the team through the next chapter of our journey."

articles.title: NASCAR Announces Last-Minute Rule Change Ahead of Phoenix Cup Series Race
articles.summary: NASCAR announced a rule change Wednesday allowing Cup Series teams to replace front brake pads and rotors at Phoenix Raceway following recent brake failures...
articles.body:
With the NASCAR Cup Series championship battle heating up, officials are making a significant change to the rules just days before Sunday's race at Phoenix Raceway.

NASCAR announced Wednesday , Oct. 14, that teams will be permitted to replace their front brake pads and rotors following Saturday's practice and qualifying sessions. The adjustment comes after a string of brake-related problems raised concerns about what could happen when the series returned to another demanding short oval.

It's an unusual exception to NASCAR's normal post-qualifying restrictions, and one that could help prevent a mechanical failure from derailing a driver's championship hopes.

NASCAR Responds to Brake Concerns Ahead of Phoenix

Brake durability has become a growing concern this season, particularly at tracks where drivers repeatedly slow their cars from high speeds.

The issue was especially noticeable at World Wide Technology Raceway on Sept. 13, when multiple Cup Series cars experienced brake failures during the Enjoy Illinois 300.

Phoenix presents a similar challenge. Its relatively flat, 1-mile layout requires heavy braking, and the Cup Series' increased horsepower package has added another variable for teams to manage.

NASCAR Cup Series Senior Managing Director Brad Moran explained the decision Wednesday on SiriusXM NASCAR Radio's "The Morning Drive."

"We've elected that we're gonna let the teams at least look at their brakes and if they need to make a pad change, which is uncommon for us to do on an impound practice," Moran said. "But we've got a procedure set up to do that."

The permission comes with specific limits. Teams can replace front brake pads and rotors after Saturday's on-track sessions, but no other brake system components may be changed under the exception.

NASCAR will also allow teams to inspect their rear rotors during Sunday's pre-race adjustment period. Any issues discovered during those inspections will be handled individually.

What the New Brake Rule Means for Sunday's NASCAR Race

Importantly, NASCAR isn't requiring teams to make any changes. It's giving them the option.

Moran said there won't be a minimum wear threshold or other specific criteria that teams must meet before replacing their front brake components.

"There's no limit," Moran said. "If a team chooses to change their brake pads, it's on them to do so. The teams are allowed to do quite a bit of work in the brake area. We're just giving the opportunity to make sure they get it right and hopefully we don't have any brake issues at Phoenix."

The timing matters for more than just safety.

Sunday's race is the seventh of 10 events in NASCAR's 2026 Chase for the Cup, with Kyle Larson holding a 49-point advantage over Denny Hamlin in the championship standings.

With only four races remaining, a brake failure could have major implications for drivers trying to close that gap.

NASCAR's decision gives teams an additional opportunity to address potential trouble before the green flag rather than discovering a problem after the race begins.

The Cup Series returns to Phoenix Raceway on Sunday, Oct. 18, with the race scheduled for 3 p.m. ET on USA Network and HBO Max.

articles.title: Brexton Busch, 11, Burned the Tires Off RCR's Parked No. 8 at Kyle Busch's Charlotte Celebration of Life
articles.summary: Richard Childress Racing's No. 8 ran on a Cup car again on Oct. 9 at Charlotte Motor Speedway, for about as long as it takes to destroy a set of tires, and t...
articles.body:
Richard Childress Racing's No. 8 ran on a Cup car again on Oct. 9 at Charlotte Motor Speedway, for about as long as it takes to destroy a set of tires, and the driver was 11 years old.

Brexton Busch started his late father's No. 8 Lucas Oil Chevrolet, waved to the grandstand and lit up the rear tires near pit entry until there was little Goodyear left. NASCAR.com's account says he then climbed onto the roof, took a checkered flag from his 4-year-old sister, Lennix, and gave the crowd Kyle Busch's post-win bow before jumping down to hug his mother and sister. It was the first time Brexton had publicly driven a Cup car, according to the same report.

That number had been off the Cup grid since May 22. The day after Busch died, RCR announced it would suspend the No. 8 and enter the car as the No. 33, saying the 8 was "reserved and ready for Brexton Busch when he is ready to go NASCAR racing." The team's statement credited Busch with helping design RCR's stylized 8.

Busch was 41. The joint statement from his family, RCR and NASCAR on May 21 called the death sudden and gave no cause. Two days later the family said severe pneumonia had progressed into sepsis.

The celebration began around 8 p.m. at the start/finish line, after Layne Riggs won the Craftsman Truck Series race, and was free to anyone at the track . WBTV reported thousands of fans stayed, and that they were handed Busch flags and rally towels. FS1 carried it live, NASCAR on FOX's Mike Joy hosted, and ten of Busch's cars were parked on display. It followed months of smaller gestures, from an empty chair at Daytona to Rowdy Road at Las Vegas Motor Speedway .

Kurt Busch, who recently bought back his 2000 Roush race truck at Mecum Nashville , opened. "I knew he was going to be fast," he said, per WBTV, describing a younger brother who wanted to do everything "bigger, better and faster than me."

Joe Gibbs, whose No. 18 Toyota Busch drove from 2008 through 2022 to two Cup titles and 56 wins, spoke, as did three drivers who came through Kyle Busch Motorsports' truck program: Daniel Suárez, Noah Gragson and Christopher Bell. Kyle Larson, the defending Cup champion, said Busch called him "Tiny Kyle" and later asked him to help coach Brexton on dirt.

Austin Dillon, Busch's teammate at RCR, kept his short: "Trophies collect dust. Records are meant to be broken."

Samantha Busch said her husband was happy at home through the winless last stretch of his Cup career, and told the grandstand, "This is not the end of Kyle's story." Country singer Cole Swindell played an acoustic set. A drone show drew the No. 18 and the number 234, Busch's win total across NASCAR's three national series, over the track where he won more than any other driver.

Richard Childress was there; NASCAR's photo gallery shows him watching. He wasn't on the speaker list, and nobody announced anything about the car his team holds for Brexton. NASCAR's coverage doesn't say whether the Chevrolet Brexton drove was a race chassis or a show car.

Nowhere in 2027, on RCR's own paperwork. On Aug. 24 the team named Austin Hill full-time driver of the No. 33 for next season, the car he has driven since the Coca-Cola 600. The renumbered entry is now a fixture, not a fill-in.

Childress went further at Michigan in June. He said the No. 8 is reserved for Brexton if he reaches the Cup Series, whether or not he drives for RCR, and that the team had planned to announce a contract extension for Busch before he died. "That kid can drive a race car," Childress said.

Neither RCR nor NASCAR has put a date on any of it, and the rulebook sets its own clock. When NASCAR lowered the O'Reilly Auto Parts Series minimum age last November, it landed at 17 for road courses and shorter ovals and 18 for the big ones. Brexton is about six years from the first of those, and the Cup Series sits a rung above that.

The next public stop is the NASCAR Hall of Fame, where the "Kyle Busch: Honoring A Legacy" exhibit is built around his 2015 championship No. 18 Camry. Samantha, Brexton and Lennix posed with that car at the unveiling. The Hall hasn't said how long the exhibit will stay up.

Should RCR leave the No. 8 parked for however many years it takes Brexton to get there, or put it back on a race car before then?

Sources: Busch family, RCR and NASCAR joint statement (May 21, 2026); RCR No. 8/No. 33 announcement (May 22, 2026); Richard Childress press conference at Michigan (June 6, 2026); RCR Austin Hill announcement (Aug. 24, 2026); NASCAR celebration of life announcement (Oct. 2, 2026), event report, video and photo gallery (Oct. 9 and 10, 2026); NASCAR O'Reilly Series eligibility rule change (Nov. 1, 2025); WBTV.

articles.title: Haas anuncia Rafael Câmara, e Brasil vai ter mais um piloto no grid | Ge
articles.standfirst: Piloto de 21 anos assume a vaga de Esteban Ocon e será companheiro do inglês Oliver Bearman na equipe. Nascido no Recife, Rafa vai ser o primeiro representante do Nordeste na categoria
articles.summary: Piloto de 21 anos assume a vaga de Esteban Ocon e será companheiro do inglês Oliver Bearman na equipe. Nascido no Recife, Rafa vai ser o primeiro representante do Nordeste na F1
articles.body:
A Fórmula 1 terá Brasil em dose dupla! A Haas anunciou nesta terça-feira (13) a contratação do pernambucano Rafael Câmara , de 21 anos de idade, para a temporada de 2027 da categoria. O jovem assinou um vínculo multianual com o time americano; portanto, está sob contrato pelo menos até o fim de 2028. Ele substitui o francês Esteban Ocon, que esteve com o time nos dois últimos anos. A repórter Mariana Becker fez uma entrevista exclusiva com o novo piloto brasileiro no grid!

Com a chegada de Câmara à Haas, o Brasil voltará a ter dois pilotos no grid da Fórmula 1 após 11 temporadas. A última vez em que isso aconteceu foi em 2016, quando Felipe Massa (Williams) e Felipe Nasr (Sauber) integravam a lista de pilotos. Rafael Câmara se junta a Gabriel Bortoleto, que quebrou o jejum de brasileiros na categoria em 2025 e compete pela Audi.

Estou muito feliz por ter alcançado o sonho. Claro que não vai acabar por aqui, mas muito contente por realizar uma parte e estar na Fórmula 1. Foram muitos anos nessa caminhada com meus pais, principalmente. Muito sacrifício, muita dedicação. Estou muito contente por eles também, por tudo que eles fizeram para fazer isso dar certo - disse o piloto, em entrevista exclusiva à comentarista da TV Globo, Mariana Becker.

Rafael Câmara é novo piloto da Haas na F1 2027 — Foto: Divulgação

O piloto nascido em Recife se tornará o 34º brasileiro a participar de uma corrida na Fórmula 1, mas com um marco especial: Rafa será o primeiro da história da região Nordeste na categoria. Entre os 33 antecessores de Rafael, 22 nasceram na região Sudeste; cinco no Sul, um no Centro-Oeste, um no Norte e quatro fora do país.

Rafael revelou na entrevista à Mariana Becker que se emocionou ao ouvir a notícia do chefe de equipe, Ayao Komatsu. O jovem piloto também contou como comunicou a novidade aos pais:

Quando eu descobri que ia ser piloto no ano que vem com o Ayao (Komatsu, chefe da Haas), quando ele me contou. Ele ligou e falou que eu iria estar no grid no ano que vem. Quando comecei a agradecer, a voz começou a embargar. Não aconteceu nada, mas com meu pai não deu para segurar. Ele veio me dar um abraço, eu falei para meu pai e minha mãe... não sabia nem como falar, não gosto muito de demonstrar emoção. Fiquei pensando 'como é que eu vou contar?'. Eu só soltei rápido e se ele entendesse, entendeu.

Eu falei assim: 'Ano que vem vou estar no grid'. Falei rápido, meu pai me olhou e deu um sorriso. Veio dar um abraço em mim. Estava eu, ele e minha mãe. A minha mãe ficou vendo ele, se abraçando. Depois dei um abraço na minha mãe também. Com meu pai eu dei uma chorada.

Rafael Câmara e Ayao Komatsu, chefe da Haas — Foto: Divulgação

Na liderança da Fórmula 2, Rafa luta pelo título com o búlgaro Nikola Tsolov e com o irlandês Alexander Dunne. O brasileiro tem os pontos necessários para a superlicença, documento exigido aos pilotos que participam da Fórmula 1, e atingiu os requisitos ao conquistar a Fórmula 3, em 2025. Ele terá como companheiro na Haas o inglês Oliver Bearman – ambos são pilotos da Academia de Jovens da Ferrari.

Rafael recebeu forte apoio da escuderia de Maranello na trajetória rumo à F1. Nesta temporada, o pernambucano pôde testar carros da equipe em pistas como Barcelona, Budapeste e Mugello e Ímola. O brasileiro foi bem avaliado internamente pelo ritmo e evolução desde os testes iniciais.

Rafael Câmara testa a Haas no Autódromo Internacional do Algarve, em Portimão, Portugal — Foto: Bruno Bede Pereira

As especulações sobre a ida de Rafael Câmara à Haas passaram a ganhar força durante a pausa de meio de temporada da Fórmula 1. A equipe americana, então, organizou um teste decisivo no Autódromo Internacional do Algarve, em Portimão, Portugal. Além de Câmara, participaram da atividade no fim de agosto o italiano Leonardo Fornaroli e o experiente japonês Ryo Hirakawa, ambos também sob avaliação. Bearman esteve no local para estabelecer um tempo de referência.

Com o VF-25, carro da equipe usado no ano passado, Rafael fez o melhor tempo do dia na atividade, superando até mesmo a marca de Bearman, conforme adiantou o jornalista Rafael Lopes, do ge.globo. O ótimo desempenho no teste e o apoio da Ferrari foram fatores importantes na escolha da Haas por Câmara, também levando em conta os benefícios financeiros que o time terá - seja por meio da Ferrari, seja pela diminuição dos custos salariais.

Rafael Câmara tem 21 anos, nascido em 5 de maio de 2005. Filho do advogado Amaro Câmara e de Paula Câmara, cresceu no bairro de Boa Viagem, no litoral da Zona Sul da capital pernambucana. Inspirado pelo irmão mais velho, começou a andar de kart indoor com apenas seis, em 2011; além disso, a avó Niege Rossiter foi pioneira em corridas no Recife.

Depois de se mudar para São Paulo e disputar campeonatos locais e nacionais a partir dos nove, ele passou a competir na Europa. Em 2020, foi bicampeão brasileiro da modalidade.

Rafael Câmara e Felipe Massa no Mundial de Kart da Finlândia — Foto: Divulgação

Até 2021, Rafael foi vice-campeão europeu, e acumulou conquistas na WSK Champions Cup e WSK Super Master Series. Os resultados que obteve com 16 anos o credenciaram para uma indicação no processo seletivo da Academia da Ferrari e, ainda em 2021, Rafa foi anunciado como novo membro da escola da escuderia, ao lado de Oliver Bearman.

No ano seguinte, o pernambucano fez sua estreia em carros de fórmula: disputou a Fórmula 4 dos Emirados Árabes Unidos, da Itália e Alemanha. Câmara faturou oito vitórias somadas nos três campeonatos, foi vice-campeão da F4 emiradense e terceiro na alemã e na italiana.

Rafael Câmara no cockpit do carro de Fórmula 4 da Prema durante testes na Europa — Foto: Ferrari Promo

Antes de migrar para a Fórmula Regional Europeia (FRECA), um dos berços de muitos titulares da Fórmula 2 e da Fórmula 1, Câmara competiu na edição do Oriente Médio da categoria em 2023 e terminou o ano em terceiro lugar na tabela. A campanha rendeu uma vaga na FRECA com a Prema ainda em 2023.

Quinto no campeonato daquele ano, o recifense seguiu com a Prema na temporada seguinte, em 2024. Começou o ano vencendo na Alemanha e iniciou uma campanha de nove vitórias e 12 pódios rumo ao título - que faturou com uma rodada de antecedência em Barcelona, na Espanha.

Rafael Câmara é campeão da temporada 2024 da Fórmula Regional European Championship by Alpine — Foto: Ferrari

Em setembro de 2024, Câmara foi anunciado como titular da Trident na F3 para 2025, e desfrutou de uma ascensão veloz na categoria: mesmo estreando com um abandono na corrida sprint da Austrália, venceu a prova principal e também levou a melhor na disputa de domingo no Bahrein. A partir daí, o pernambucano embalou no campeonato e conquistou o título com uma rodada de antecedência, na Hungria.

Rafael Câmara terminou o campeonato de 2025 com quatro vitórias, além de ter registrado um feito inédito na Fórmula 3 ao largar cinco vezes na pole position. O recifense encerrou a temporada com 166 pontos, contra 124 do vice-líder Nikola Tsolov. A excelente temporada lhe rendeu o prêmio de Novato do Ano, entregue pela Federação Internacional de Automobilismo (FIA) em uma cerimônia realizada em dezembro.

Rafael Câmara foi campeão da Fórmula 3 na temporada 2025 — Foto: Malcolm Griffiths/F1 via Getty Images

Câmara herdou a vaga deixada na Invicta Racing por Leonardo Fornaroli, campeão da Fórmula 2 em 2025. Depois de ir ao pódio nas duas primeiras etapas do ano, na Austrália e em Miami, Rafael voltou a terminar entre os três primeiros na quinta corrida, desta vez no topo: o pernambucano ganhou a primeira na F2 na prova principal em Barcelona.

Com términos frequentes na zona de pontuação, Rafael conseguiu mais duas vitórias, em Spa-Francorchamps e Baku, além de outros dois pódios: foi terceiro na corrida principal na Hungria e segundo em Monza. Os resultados o catapultaram à liderança do campeonato, com 207 pontos contra 200 de Tsolov e 189 de Dunne. Ainda restam duas etapas para o fim da Fórmula 2, no Catar e em Abu Dhabi.

articles.title: Incêndio após curto-circuito atinge escola no Sul do Piauí | G1
articles.standfirst: Não houve registro de feridos, e as chamas foram controladas pela equipe da Brigada Municipal com o apoio de moradores da região.
articles.summary: Um princípio de incêndio em escola no Piauí foi controlado pela Brigada Municipal e moradores após curto-circuito em Cristino Castro; não houve feridos.
articles.body:
Um curto-circuito atingiu a Escola Francisco Miranda, em Cristino Castro , no Sul do Piauí, na manhã desta quinta-feira (15) por volta das 9h. No momento em que o fogo foi registrado, não havia alunos em aula. Não houve registro de vítimas.

O coordenador da Defesa Civil de Cristino Castro, Bruno Nascimento, conhecido como Bruno Bombeiro, informou ao g1 que o fogo começou após um curto-circuito no contador e se espalhou pelo painel de ACM (Material Composto de Alumínio) do portão da escola.

A Brigada Municipal atuou no combate às chamas com o apoio de moradores da região. As causas da sobrecarga elétrica ainda deverão ser apuradas.

"Teve um curto-circuito, onde levou a um princípio de incêndio no contador, passando para estrutura do portão da escola. Graças a Deus, ao morador e à Brigada Municipal, o incêndio foi controlado com sucesso, e totalmente sem grandes perdas e sem vítimas", disse Bruno.

A direção da escola informou que não havia aulas no momento da ocorrência. Segundo a instituição, não havia alunos nem funcionários no local, já que as atividades estavam suspensas por causa do feriado do Dia do Professor.

A escola continua sem energia elétrica, mas a direção esclareceu que a Secretaria de Estado da Educação (Seduc) já tomou conhecimento da situação e encaminhou uma equipe técnica da rede para atender a ocorrência.

A previsão para o restabelecimento da energia e para a retomada das atividades na escola será informada após a avaliação da equipe técnica enviada ao local.

articles.title: Lo que no se vio de Marc Márquez en Indonesia: "Acabé bien, pero no delante"
articles.standfirst: El 'Inside' de Ducati refleja la alegría por la victoria del Sprint y la pasión de los fans
articles.summary: El 'Inside' de Ducati refleja la alegría por la victoria del Sprint y la pasión de los fans
articles.body: El ‘Inside’ (desde dentro) de Ducati del Gran Premio de Indonesia de MotoGP refleja la pasión de los fans locales, la enorme alegría por la victoria inesperada de Marc Márquez en el Sprint, más decepciones de Pecco Bagnaia o el buen sabor de boca final del ‘93’ pese a su sexto en carrera y el pleno de Aprilia en el ‘top 4’. La cita empieza con los numerosos eventos a los que acuden los pilotos. Marc tiene uno, con Shell, en el que los niños le mandan ánimos. “Tienen más o menos, pero siempre son felices. Tienen esa felicidad, son creyentes”, resume. Al hablar con los medios, el jueves, el primer tema es el cambio en el formato de MotoGP para 2027. Pecco lo habla con Jack Miller. “A mí me gusta”, dice el turinés. “Ya, pero ¿y el ‘warm up’”? Suelta el australiano. “Eso lo hablaremos”, replica el ‘63’. Con los primeros entrenamientos del viernes, Bagnaia empieza a sufrir, aunque menos que otras veces. El mayor de los Márquez coge energía bebiendo sales minerales. “¿Ese es más fuerte?”, le espeta un mecánico. “Es blanco, es para hacer las paces con Mandalika”, bromea, sabedor de que es su pista maldita, donde nunca había acabado un domingo. Luego, ya hablan más en serio. “La pista va cogiendo goma y es mejor para nosotros, especialmente para mí, sobre todo desde que confío mucho en el ángulo de inclinación”, confiesa. “Hemos mejorado”, admite el de Chivasso a Gigi Dall’Igna tras pasar directo a la Q2. En el vídeo se contempla una conversación entre Tardozzi y Marc. El jefe de equipo le da sugerencias sobre posicionar su cuerpo de forma diferente para lograr más tracción, que es donde Aprilia los gana. “No es la configuración, soy yo”, reconoce el de Cervera. Llega la primera satisfacción, al ser cuarto en la Q2, tras seguir a Martinator. “Buena estrategia, Riga”, le dice un mecánico a Rigamonti, el jefe técnico. “Bien, cometí algunos errores. La adrenalina me estaba saltando”, suelta el catalán. Pecco bromea por una investigación de los comisarios. “Descalificado, nos volvemos a casa”, ironiza en el box. “No podía hacer otra cosa”, añade. El Sprint desata la locura en Ducati, con Marc ganando y Jorge, con problemas, además del golpe entre Bezzecchi y Raúl Fernández. “Presión de los neumáticos”, detectan al momento en el garaje ‘rosso’ al ver a Martinator dejarse pasar. El ‘93’ estaba agotado. “Hasta me he dado un baño”, desvela al volver al box y de darse un baño de masas. El domingo por la mañana, varios pilotos ‘comentan la jugada’, entre ellos Marc y Martín. “Éste se puso las botas”, suelta el vigente campeón. “Yo decía: ‘No hacen la curva ni de coña’”, replica el madrileño. Álex y Marc ven que la celebración de Máximo Quiles en Moto3 fue como estaba planeado. “Qué bonito”, dice Gemma, la novia del ‘93’. “A lo campeón”, le suelta el del Ducati oficial tras pararle en el ‘pit lane’. “Máximo será un gran piloto en el futuro y estoy muy orgulloso del trabajo que está haciendo”, dice Marc a cámara. Bagnaia está hundido tras caerse en la carrera dominical. “Lo siento”, dice a su equipo al regresar. Marc es sexto y es recibido entre tímidos aplausos. “Bien. Sí, larga. Parecía que no acababa nunca”, afirma. El mayor de los Márquez se topa con Acosta. “Estaba jodidísimo con las presiones de los neumáticos. Cuando te adelanté, pensé: ‘Ya está’. Luego, me volvió de nuevo y pensé: ‘Otra vez, no’. Tú, ¿qué tal? ¿Mal también?”, le suelta. “No, yo he acabado bien, pero no delante”, replica. Luego, ante la prensa, el leridano certifica que no ha sido un mal fin de semana.

articles.title: Carlos Tatay apunta al Dakar 2028: “Está muy cerca”
articles.standfirst: El piloto, que sufrió un accidente brutal hace tres años que le dejó en silla de ruedas, se prepara en la Vuelva Ciclorurista a Ibiza Campagnolo para su gran reto en buggy
articles.summary: El piloto, que sufrió un accidente brutal hace tres años que le dejó en silla de ruedas, se prepara en la Vuelva Ciclorurista a Ibiza Campagnolo para su gran reto en buggy
articles.body: Cuando hace menos de tres años Carlos Tatay tuvo aquel maldito accidente en el circuito de Portimao el mundo se detuvo. Su moto se estrelló a más de 200 kilómetros por hora y las lesiones fueros irreversibles en la médula. Su lucha ha sido titánica y siempre ha mantenido ese espíritu de deportista profesional con el que se había hecho hueco en el Mundial de motociclismo. Ha pelado contra todo, incluso contra una FIM que en principio no le consideró "inválido" para intentar ahorrarse pagarle al piloto español las indemnizaciones correspondientes. Sentado en su propio tipo de bici adaptada a Carlos se le derrama la energía. “Objetivo Dakar 2028”, comenta de forma rotunda. “Ya tengo todo el orden y está muy bien enfocada la cosa”, añade. “Este año haré el Rally de Marruecos y pruebas en España y así llegaré con kilómetros”. Su ambición es tremenda y dice que es complicado verle perder la sonrisa. Tras superar el trauma inicial del accidente, "me empieza a gustar mi nueva vida", dijo en MARCA, Carlos Tatay siempre ha querido medirse, volver al motor, dar gas. “Siempre busqué competir con gente sin discapacidad y en el motor es en el único sitio en el que se puede hacer… y ganar”. Desde hace un tiempo compite en rally y no defrauda, tiene talento de sobra. Su objetivo del Dakar, a los mandos de un buggy, está cerca, mucho. A Ibiza, Carlos ha llegado con una bici que llama la atención. Se la fabricó a medida un artesano con alas de avión de fibra de carbono y en la carretera vuela. La vuelta cicloturista a Ibiza Campagnolo le invitó a participar este año y se lo ha pasado en grande. Incluso tuvo la oportunidad de rodar con el mítico Miguel Indurain. “El ciclismo me sirve mucho para entrenar y estar en forma todo el año”, asegura a MARCA antes de partir a recorrer las carreteras de la isla blanca con el Dakar en la cabeza. “Ir sin acumular kilómetros sería un suicidio. 2028 es el gran objetivo y creo que allí estaré”. Con 23 años Tatay se llevó un golpe duro siendo casi un niño, pero el destino y su capacidad de superación le han abierto nuevas puertas por las que se ha volado sin preguntar…. Como un avión como el que han utilizado para fabricar superación bicicleta.

articles.title: Formula 1: The pit stop that helped save lives
articles.summary: How an F1 pit stop inspired changes to hospital care that have helped save lives ever since.
articles.body:
When the McLaren pit crew refuelled a car, changed its tyres and relayed information to their driver in less than seven seconds at the Spanish Grand Prix in 2001, they were just doing their jobs.

But 700 miles away in the break room at Great Ormond Street Hospital (GOSH), Dr Martin Elliott and his colleagues were watching after completing a life-saving operation on a young child.

The brief glimpse would change how the doctors approached patient care. From surgery-to-ICU handovers and neonatal care to air-ambulance response times, F1's innovations have made an impact far beyond the track.

At Ferrari's factory in Maranello, the GOSH medical team studied how pit crews organised roles, communication and handovers.

Doctors and nurses started each procedure with a checklist, setting out specific roles and tasks. This reduced human error and helped ensure key tasks were completed. All patient data was also shared from the operating theatre to the care unit.

Gaps in performance were identified and addressed, while repeated rehearsals helped refine the process.

As a result, the process from surgery to intensive care became more organised, and a 2007 study by researchers at GOSH and the University of Oxford found the F1-inspired handover process reduced technical errors, information omissions and handover time.

Reflecting on the project, Dr Elliott, then a consultant paediatric cardiothoracic surgeon at GOSH, said: "The environment we were working in then and in many ways still do is fundamentally potentially dangerous at every step.

"And of course, fundamentally, that's how F1 doesn't make mistakes. They have created an environment of complete precision, not only in engineering, but also in process, because they simply can't afford financially or from a race perspective to slip up.

"It's the same, you know, the precious parcel on the trolley is the same as the precious parcel in the car. You have to get all of those steps right."

The model was later adopted by other healthcare teams.

Fifteen years ago, Williams worked with the University Hospital of Wales to improve neonatal resuscitation.

Former Williams human performance specialist Gemma Fisher recognised that the organisation of pit-crew equipment to prevent delay could also be applied in a hospital setting.

Video analysis unveiled the chaotic reality of medical emergencies with overlapping voices and misplaced equipment.

Standardising roles - deciding who stood where, who needed to be heard at what moment and where equipment was stationed - allowed for a faster, more efficient response.

Debriefings allowed medical staff to review what had happened and identify what could be improved for future emergencies.

The changes also encouraged junior doctors to raise concerns without fear of blame.

The collaboration extended beyond working practices and into engineering. Advanced Healthcare Technology and Williams have since developed the Babypod: a carbon fibre carrier designed to withstand a 20G crash, which can help prevent injury in the transportation of babies from ambulance to hospital.

F1 continues to find new ways to apply its expertise in emergency medicine.

At this year's race at Silverstone, a collaboration with Air Ambulance Cornwall showed how response times could be improved, with take-off time reduced from five minutes to three and a half.

This was achieved using many of the same methods, including quick and organised starts, having equipment ready for use and clear communication across the team.

David Richards, chairman of Motorsport UK and former team principal of BAR and Benetton, said: "You might not see one and a half minutes in the overall scheme of things, but one and a half minutes when you're lying by the side of the road or you've fallen off a horse or you've fallen down a cliff and you've hurt yourself, those minutes must seem like years for the person who's injured."

Richards said the partnership would continue to look for ways to reduce response times further.

Twenty-five years after Dr Elliott first saw a pit stop that inspired a new way of thinking, lessons from the sport continue to influence healthcare, from neonatal treatment to emergency response.

articles.title: Colapinto pide cordura: "Hay veces que nos pasamos de la raya"
articles.standfirst: El argentino lanza un comunicado a sus fans por redes sociales exigiendo respeto
articles.summary: El argentino lanza un comunicado a sus fans por redes sociales exigiendo respeto
articles.body: "Ya tendría que haber hablado con todos ustedes. Es algo necesario que tenemos que cambiar y mejorar". Así comenzaba el vídeo posteado en redes sociales el piloto argentino en el que pedía cordura y sensatez todos sus fans, con el fin de que cesasen los ataques por parte de los argentinos hacia otros miembros del Mundial de Fórmula 1. No obstante, en los más de dos minutos que dura el vídeo, el piloto de Alpine ha podido tocar varios palos dirigiéndose a sus fans. Entre ellos, el argentino agradece, sobre todas las cosas, el apoyo que recibe de parte de los suyos, calificándose a sí mismo de afortunado por haberlos tenido desde el principio, sumado a la gente que se va uniendo a 'bancarle' con su sueño. El argentino ha hecho referencia a cómo le empujan y le ayudan con ese apoyo a conseguir los resultados y a seguir creciendo. "... hay veces que nos pasamos de la raya y, en vez de apoyarme, terminamos criticando. Atacando a otros pilotos, colegas, compañeros de equipo, a mis mecánicos, ingenieros, etc. Gente con la que trabajo día a día", continuó el argentino. Y es que, tal y como él mismo ha relatado, piensan que le están haciendo un favor y, en realidad, es todo lo contrario. "Necesito que me ayuden a parar esto todos juntos. Tenemos que mejorar como sociedad y ayudarme así a tener una mejor actuación y seguir consiguiendo mis sueños", zanjaba el Argentino. Del mismo modo, Colapinto, ha podido comunicar su decisión de alejarse de las pantallas y centrarse en su carrera deportiva y en mejorar. Toda la situación que lleva viviendo durante varias semanas ha terminado por colapsar al de Alpine, tomando así tal drástica decisión, con el fin de poder descansar y estar más tranquilo en su día a día. Este vídeo ha sido aplaudido por varios, Lando Norris o Flavio Briatore entre otros, ensalzando así la determinación que los pilotos deben tener a la hora de comunicarse a sus fans y pedir respeto hacia sus compañeros, sabiendo que son los únicos que pueden hacerlo.

articles.title: Red Bull cierra su etapa tormentosa y renueva al jefe de Verstappen
articles.standfirst: Laurent Mekies seguirá al frente del equipo Red Bull a pesar de la difícil temporada
articles.summary: Laurent Mekies seguirá al frente del equipo Red Bull a pesar de la difícil temporada
articles.body: Numerosas son las dudas que han ido recayendo sobre Mekies a lo largo de este difícil temporada en Red Bull desde que accedió al puesto de Jefe de Equipo en julio del año pasado, tras la destitución de Horner. Un cambio de reglamento y un motor construido por ellos mismos, con las dificultades que eso supone, son parte de los problemas a los que el francés ha tenido que hacer frente en una de las temporadas más difíciles que se recuerdan de la Fórmula1 y tras sentarse al frente del equipo austriaco, de una forma un tanto peculiar como polémica. Aún y así, los austriacos comienzan a conseguir esos resultados a los que están acostumbrados y parece que la paz y la concordia vuelve a reinar en Red Bull, haciendo que Mekies haya firmado una extensión de contrato hasta 2031 con Red Bull, acompañando a Verstappen, y Hadjar unas cuantas temporadas más. Esta renovación llega, al igual que su ascenso, en un momento bastante turbulento, protagonizado por la misma persona: Christian Horner. El ex-jefe de equipo de Red Bull, quien llevaba más de 20 años al frente de los austriacos, fue inesperada e injustificadamente despedido, abriendo paso al ascenso de Mekies, quien tomó las riendas del equipo y, cuyo buen hacer, a pesar de las dificultades, ha tenido su recompensa. Del mismo modo, las declaraciones de Horner parecen no haber afectado en ninguna toma de decisión y, menos aún, en la forma que Mekies ha tenido de proceder al frente del equipo. El británico, quien recientemente ha publicado su biografía y concedido entrevistas al respecto, ha ido aclarando qué fue exactamente lo que sucedió con Red Bull y sus pretensiones con Ferrari. A raíz de dichas declaraciones se empezó a extender el rumor sobre quién realmente tiene el poder en Red Bull. "Helmut podía ser muy directo y me decepcionó que se hubiera quedado como invitado en nuestra casa dos días antes (de su despido) sin dar ninguna pista de que esto iba a suceder", declaró el inglés en una entrevista a The Guardian. De este modo, Horner explicó la lucha interna que se dio entre Helmunt Marko y Jos Verstappen por hacerse con ese vacío de poder que dejó Dietrich Mateschitz, tras su fallecimiento en 2022. Horner puso en entredicho el papel que juega verdaderamente Mekies en Red Bull y sobre quien tiene el poder dentro del equipo, siendo muchos los que postulan al padre del tetracampeón como el 'jefe encubierto'. Sin embargo, el Jefe de Equipo de los austriacos hace oídos sordos a tales rumores y sigue enfocado en su trabajo. "Me siento increíblemente orgulloso de continuar este viaje con Oracle Red Bull Racing, y me gustaría dar las gracias a Chalerm (Yoovidhya), Mark (Mateschitz) y Oliver (Mintzlaff), a todo el equipo y a todas las personas implicadas por la confianza que han depositado en el proyecto", declaraba Mekies tras su renovación.

articles.title: Alonso, Verstappen y Red Bull, el fichaje imposible de la Fórmula 1
articles.standfirst: La 'bomba' que la biografía de Christian Horner ('Drive', 2026) soltó pudo haber cambiado la historia reciente del Gran Circo
articles.summary: La biografía de Horner ('Drive', 2026) reabrió una posibilidad que no se concretó y pudo acabar con el asturiano en el equipo de las bebidas energéticas
articles.body: Christian Horner, en su plano de figura omnipotente en el paddock de Fórmula 1 por más que ya se ha cumplido un año desde su salida del puesto de CEO de Red Bull, devolvió a la palestra un viejo debate del Gran Circo tras la publicación de su autobiografía (Drive, 2026). En sus páginas, el ingeniero y dirigente trató los posibles fichajes de su antiguo equipo que no se terminaron de dar, con posibilidad de llamar a la puerta de Charles Leclerc, Carlos Sainz y el bombazo de Fernando Alonso. Porque no era la primera vez en la que quería, de verdad, al bicampeón. Y porque pudo formarse una pareja histórica en la F1 junto a Max Verstappen. El británico profundiza en el libro sobre esa toma de decisiones para cerrar un fichaje. Tanto las negociaciones, las conversaciones dentro del paddock y el factor determinante que Horner desvela como vital para entender que Alonso y Verstappen sólo sean una pareja soñada y no una de las que más renombre tienen en la F1 junto a los Prost-Senna, Alonso-Hamilton o Hamilton-Leclerc en la era moderna de la clase reina. Alonso no fichó por Red Bull, cuenta el antiguo CEO, por la presión de una cúpula del equipo que lideraba Helmut Marko y el entorno de Verstappen, en la que el eje central es el padre del tetracampeón, Jos. No es un asunto menor, pues su poder era total en la estructura de Milton Keynes. En esos cursos de gloria en el equipo de las bebidas energéticas formaban la columna vertebral de un proyecto ganador que justo después... murió de éxito. Y también puede explicar la negativa al asturiano. Entre 2024 y 2025 se marcharon piezas claves (Newey, Wheatley...), la relación con Verstappen se desgastó y se han necesitado dos temporadas para devolver la plena confianza al holandés. Por un lado, Alonso era un gallo en el corral que Red Bull no aceptó tener y buscaban todos los focos en Max. Por temor a la competencia, por preferir a un segundo piloto claro o por esa filosofía del equipo que todavía sigue presente. Lo único seguro es que Verstappen no tuvo que ver. "Supe que no era su petición", admitió Horner. "Helmut [Marko] me dijo que lo entusiasmaba la idea de Alonso]", añadió. "Yo pensaba que era el piloto perfecto para nosotros", rememora Horner. No era la primera vez, y ya entre 2009 y 2010 quiso que pilotase para su equipo, pero Ferrari encabezaba la lista de preferencias del asturiano desde todo el jaleo de McLaren en 2007. En 2024 y 2025 no estuvo tan lejos, pero la pareja se convirtió en un imposible. Posteriormente, Alonso afianzó su relación con Aston Martin y su unión se convirtió en algo más que una simple combinación de equipo-piloto. El asturiano se volcó con el equipo británico, su vinculación va más allá del propio contrato y se abre a otros frentes con la participación en el Dakar como guinda o una posible salida a las 24 Horas de Le Mans. Pero, al mismo tiempo, el asturiano no recaló en un proyecto que siempre ha ganado. Desde ese 2024, Red Bull colecciona 18 victorias (todas de Verstappen) entre el cuarto título del holandés, la persecución a Norris y Piastri de 2025 que llegó hasta la última bandera a cuadros y un 2026 en el que su nuevo motor sí ha funcionado. En paralelo, Aston Martin no ha vuelto a pisar el podio desde la épica resolución de Brasil 2023 entre Alonso y Pérez. Y vive una incertidumbre notable con un motor Honda que está muy lejos de las referencias en la F1. Es una de esa clase de decisiones que pudo haber cambiado todo de raíz. Pero que se convertirá en sólo una posibilidad. La lógica dice que a Alonso se le preguntará en la próxima comparecencia por la biografía de Horner. Y que quizá en Red Bull alguien ofrezca más motivos claros para la negativa a formar equipo. Eso sí, ahora suenan más fuerte aquellas palabras de Helmut Marko sobre el piloto español. "Tuvimos conversaciones, pero es importante tener un ambiente de trabajo en armonía para Max y con Alonso, probablemente, no hubiese sido el caso", lanzó en 2024. Visto en perspectiva, quizá tiene más peso del que un día se le dio. Es la pareja imposible.

articles.title: Franco Morbidelli on securing most coveted WSBK ride: 'Clearly Ducati has some trust in me'
articles.summary: The VR46 rider was upbeat about his impending move to World Superbike - and grateful his poor form did not cost him the chance
articles.body:
Departing MotoGP rider Franco Morbidelli has thanked Ducati for showing faith in him as he moves to its factory World Superbike team.

The Italian has endured a tough run in the VR46 MotoGP Ducati team , losing the confidence that made him a three-time winner back in 2020.

His dip in form led to him failing to find a MotoGP contract for 2027, but Ducati kept him in the fold with the factory World Superbike ride. The move is a straight swap with World Superbike champion Nicolo Bulega, who will make his full-time MotoGP debut with VR46 next season.

Speaking ahead of this weekend's Indonesian Grand Prix, Morbidelli said he was aware he had not made himself an obvious choice for Ducati given his declining performance - not to mention a reputation for getting involved in incidents on the track.

"I'm happy about the chance I got from Ducati," said the 31-year-old, whose bike will carry a special Garuda-themed livery at the Indonesian GP. "It's not easy because after a year like this last one it's not easy to choose me. But clearly Ducati has some trust in the job that I can do and I'm really grateful about that."

The Roman referenced quotes by Ducati's general manager Gigi Dall'Igna at the time of the announcement, and the fact that World Superbikes will switch to Michelin rubber next season - another straight swap as Pirelli takes over as MotoGP supplier. Morbidelli will thus bring familiarity with the French company's products to his Superbike role.

"I read the words that Gigi said about me and I completely agree with him," he added. "I'm really thankful about those words and that's what I will try to bring. I'll try to bring my experience with the Michelin, and my speed, which on many occasions I had.

"If I get back to fight for the victory, I'll bring my way to fight for the victory. I had that for half of my Moto2 career and in MotoGP I had it for two years. I had the chance to fight for the victory for two years."

Another departing MotoGP race rider, Maverick Vinales, was somewhat less at peace with the idea of a move to another series, and claimed 'not to have given up yet' in his pre-Indonesian GP debrief.

articles.title: La Fórmula 1 deja 545 millones en Madrid y el Mutua Madrid Open prepara una ampliación de 8.500 plazas
articles.standfirst: El Gran Premio supera en un 21% las previsiones económicas, genera 11.000 empleos y refuerza junto al tenis el tirón prémium de la capital según se explicó en un acto de Expansión que estuvo presidido por Urbano Cairo, presidente y propietario de RCS MediaGroup
articles.summary: El Gran Premio supera en un 21% las previsiones económicas, genera 11.000 empleos y refuerza junto al tenis el tirón prémium de la capital según se explicó en un acto de Expansión que estuvo presidido por Urbano Cairo, presidente y propietario de RCS MediaGroup
articles.body: Madrid ha encontrado en la Fórmula 1 y el Mutua Madrid Open dos escaparates capaces de mover mucho más que deporte. El rugido de los monoplazas y el golpeo de una pelota de tenis arrastran visitantes, empresas, turismo, hostelería, transporte y marcas de lujo. Ese fue el terreno común que compartieron José Vicente de los Mozos, presidente del Comité Ejecutivo de IFEMA Madrid y promotor del Gran Premio de España de Fórmula 1, y Gérard Tsobanian, consejero delegado del Mutua Madrid Open, durante el EXPANSIÓN Luxury Forum, que cuenta con la colaboración de Círculo Fortuny y 'Fuera de Serie', y el apoyo de Puig, Santander, DILS LucasFox, Radisson Hotel Group y Mckinsey & Company, como knowledge partner. El acto estuvo presidido por Urbano Cairo, presidente y propietario de RCS MediaGroup. La Fórmula 1 puso las cifras más contundentes sobre la mesa. De los Mozos anunció que la primera edición del Gran Premio de España celebrada en Madrid generó un impacto económico de 545 millones de euros, frente a los 450 millones calculados inicialmente. La diferencia supone superar las previsiones en un 21%. "El impacto para Madrid lo ciframos inicialmente en 450 millones, y hoy puedo anunciar en primicia que son 545 millones de euros", aseguró. "Cada euro generado en el GP ha tenido un retorno de cuatro euros en la economía madrileña", dijo De los Mozos. El empleo también quedó por encima de lo esperado. "De 8.900 empleos previstos llegamos a 11.000 empleos", señaló. El directivo añadió otra referencia para medir el alcance económico de la cita: "cada euro generado en el Gran Premio ha tenido un retorno de cuatro euros en la economía madrileña". El impacto salió además del circuito y alcanzó de lleno al turismo y los servicios de la ciudad. Según las cifras expuestas por el presidente del Comité Ejecutivo de IFEMA Madrid, la ocupación hostelera alcanzó el 85% durante el Gran Premio, mientras que la hostelería y el transporte concentraron más de 100 millones de euros de actividad económica. "Humildemente contribuimos como uno de los motores económicos de Madrid", afirmó. A ese movimiento se sumó el negocio generado alrededor de las empresas y las marcas internacionales que acudieron a la carrera. Uno de los focos estuvo en las zonas de hospitalidad. El Gran Premio reunió a unas 19.000 personas diarias en estos espacios, incluido el Paddock Club. Allí conviven invitados, clientes, empresas y firmas que utilizan la Fórmula 1 como punto de encuentro y plataforma de visibilidad. De los Mozos avanzó además mejoras en estas instalaciones para la próxima edición, con la intención de reforzar una parte del evento que ya ocupa un lugar central en su propuesta comercial. El tenis también quiere ganar metros y público. Gérard Tsobanian anunció que el Mutua Madrid Open ha alcanzado un acuerdo con el Ayuntamiento de Madrid para construir un nuevo estadio dentro del recinto de la Caja Mágica. La nueva instalación añadirá 8.500 localidades al aforo actual y permitirá responder a una demanda de entradas que continúa creciendo. El tirón internacional del torneo explica buena parte de esa ampliación. Según Tsobanian, el 40% de los compradores de entradas procede de fuera de España. El Mutua Madrid Open llegará además en 2027 a su 25 aniversario y la organización aprovechará esa fecha para renovar su oferta de hospitalidad, con el objetivo de reforzar la experiencia de los asistentes y acompañar el crecimiento del torneo. Fórmula 1 y tenis comparten ahí una de sus grandes vías de crecimiento. De los Mozos puso el acento en la capacidad del Gran Premio para generar contactos empresariales y llevar visitantes a Madrid. Tsobanian incidió en el valor de estos espacios para que las firmas de lujo conecten directamente con consumidores de alto poder adquisitivo. La grada importa, pero alrededor de ella también se juega una parte cada vez mayor del negocio. Madrid reúne así dos acontecimientos con capacidad para ensanchar su impacto mucho más allá de la competición. La Fórmula 1 ya ha dejado 545 millones de euros, 11.000 empleos, una ocupación hostelera del 85% y más de 100 millones de actividad en hostelería y transporte. El Mutua Madrid Open prepara mientras una nueva pista con 8.500 localidades y una renovación de su hospitalidad de cara a 2027, con un 40% de sus compradores llegando desde fuera de España.

articles.title: Franco Colapinto: Alpine driver urges fans to stop online abuse amid concerns it is damaging his career
articles.summary: Franco Colapinto's Alpine team have had to condemn online abuse on several occasions following contentious incidents involving the Argentine driver; watch every session of the United States GP in Austin on October 23-25, live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
After becoming the first Argentine driver to compete in F1 for more than 20 years when he was drafted in by Williams midway through the 2024 season, Colapinto has received huge support from his home nation.

However, since Colapinto joined Alpine in 2025, the team have had to issue several statements condemning online hate and abuse following incidents involving the 23-year-old driver.

Colapinto had previously spoken out against online abuse but suggested on several occasions that it was a societal issue rather than a specific problem with his fanbase. His position now appears to have changed.

In a video posted on social media, Colapinto said: "Hello everyone. There's something very important that I've needed to talk to you about for some time.

"I probably should have spoken to all of you sooner, but this is something that needs to be addressed, something we need to change and improve.

"I will always be grateful, and I genuinely feel incredibly fortunate to have had you all supporting me from the very beginning.

"I'm grateful for all the support you give me, for how you help me achieve results, and for how you constantly push me to aim higher.

"You help me and the team achieve our results, race after race, day after day, as we train and try to improve. And I'm genuinely grateful for all of that.

"I know it makes you incredibly proud when things go well for me, when I score points for myself and the team. And I have always been very grateful for that support.

"Instead of supporting me, we end up criticising people and attacking other drivers, other colleagues, my team-mates, my mechanics, my engineers - people I work with every single day.

"I know you think you're defending me, but you're actually doing the opposite. You're not helping me or my future."

There have been several notable incidents of drivers facing online abuse in situations that appeared to be related to Colapinto's fanbase.

There was major hostility towards Jack Doohan at the start of the 2025 season before Alpine replaced the Australian driver with Colapinto after just six rounds.

Then, during the 2026 season, FIA race stewards were abused after Colapinto received a penalty at the Dutch Grand Prix, before his team-mate Pierre Gasly hit out at "disturbing" threats he received following the Spanish Grand Prix in September.

Reigning world champion Lando Norris then received abuse after making heavily critical comments about Colapinto after the Argentine caused a crash that took him out of the race during the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

Norris later apologised for his comments about Colapinto, but Alpine once more issued a statement condemning social media abuse.

In August, Alpine confirmed a one-year contract extension for Colapinto to remain with the team for the 2027 season.

He responded well to that news with points-scoring results in Italy and Spain at the start of September, but has failed to score at the three races since.
